This part gets you on your feet: what this manual contains, how to install the system, what you see the first time you launch a world, and what each area of the screen is for. The gamemaster (the GM) reads all of it; the player can settle for chapter 0.4.

This manual describes Shadowrun 5 (unofficial), version 1.0, as it is played: a fan project derived from shadowfoundry's system, which adds its own features and fixes to it. It does not copy the rules: it gives the page of the book where to read them, and says what the system does with them.

All

What it is for

This manual teaches you to play Shadowrun 5 in Foundry with Shadowrun 5 (unofficial): where to click, what the system computes for you, what it leaves you to do by hand. It assumes you know the rules of Shadowrun 5 and the basic gestures of Foundry (opening a sheet, dragging an item); it assumes no knowledge of code.

About this English edition

This edition is a translation of the French manual. Its screenshots were taken in French: the buttons and windows you see in them carry French labels. The text quotes each label as it appears in Foundry set to English, so match a screenshot by its layout and its icons rather than by its words.

The page references point to the English editions of the books (Core Rulebook, Run & Gun, Kill Code…). They were converted from the French editions, whose page numbers differ; if a reference lands one page off, the rule is on the neighbouring page. The system's own cards, roll windows and help still cite the French page numbers, so a page given by Foundry can differ from the one given here by a few pages. The system's wiki, linked here and there, is written in French; its entry pages also exist in English (wiki: English home page).

Reader badges

Each chapter carries, under its title, a badge that tells who it is meant for:

  • All: the GM as well as the player.

  • GM: the settings, the rule locks and the gamemaster's tools. Nothing in them is secret: a player who knows what the GM ticked understands a refusal better.

  • Player: what happens on your character's sheet.

How to read it

  1. Once, before playing: this part 0, then the chapter for your role. The GM also reads part 8 (settings and tools); the player reads part 2 (the sheet and rolls), then the part for their archetype (magic, Matrix, rigging).

  2. At the table: look up the button or the window in the table of contents; each chapter begins with "What it is for" and ends with its settings and references.

  3. In Foundry: this manual also exists as a compendium of journals, "Shadowrun 5 Manual". Each part has its MENU page there, and each page ends with a line leading back (Backlinks) to the MENU.

References and boxes

  • The rules are not copied. A page of the book is cited in italics, for example (Core Rulebook p. 49): the book is authoritative, this manual only says what the system does with it. When the book does not decide and a choice was made for the system, the text says so in one line.

  • Boxes like this one give a tip or a warning:

Good to know

The system's wiki describes each feature exhaustively, with its edge cases. This manual walks you through them; it refers to the wiki for the detail (wiki: home).

House Rules — an example

This box flags a rule that no book gives, offered by a setting or by a module. The system itself applies the book; House Rules only come into play if the GM decides so.

Backlinks: @UUID[.97e4IWOiXu7XAeW3]{MENU}

@UUID[.K6CX2EasFO6vz6Be]{0.2 Installing and updating} →

GM

What it is for

Shadowrun 5 (unofficial) installs in Foundry like any other system, from a manifest link. It carries the same identifier (sr5) as the official Shadowrun 5 system: installing it replaces the official version on your Foundry.

Before you start

  • Foundry VTT version 13 (the system does not work in version 12).

  • Chrome, Microsoft Edge or the Foundry application; Firefox is less tested.

  • The manifest link: https://github.com/DjamZee/sr5-unofficial/releases/latest/download/system.json. It always leads to the latest version: once the system is installed, Foundry offers the updates by itself.

Step by step: installing

  1. On Foundry's setup screen, open the Game Systems tab, then click Install System.

  2. At the bottom of the window, paste the link into the Manifest URL field, then click the install button.

  3. In the Game Worlds tab, click Create World and choose the Shadowrun 5 system.

Step by step: updating

  1. Back up your world first: copy the Data/worlds/<world name> folder somewhere else.

  2. Install the new version from its manifest link, as above: each prerelease has its own link, and Foundry does not find it on its own.

  3. Open the world. A migration may run on the first launch: let it finish without reloading the page. One of them rewrites once the description of every character and every NPC of the world: that is why the backup of step 1 matters.

Bringing in a Foundry V12 sheet

A sheet exported from a Foundry V12 world (right-click on the actor → Export Data) carries over as is into V13:

  1. In the V13 world, create an actor of the same type (character, NPC…).

  2. Right-click it in the Actors tab → Import Data, and choose the exported file.

  3. Open the sheet: attributes, skills, items and effects are those of V12. On the way, the system took back the description (V12 stored it elsewhere), replaced the V12 item icons with today's, and restored the Physical limit of Locksmith (Core Rulebook p. 145).

A V12 world opened in V13 receives the same repairs on its first launch, and a sheet already in V13 is left alone. A sheet imported with a prerelease older than mid-October 2026 has already lost its description: import it again from the file.

Going back to an earlier version

Reinstall the old version from its own manifest link, then open the world again from the backup made before the update. Never get the system from a clone of the repository: it would lack its styles.

Recommended modules

None is required. Each has its own entry in part 9.

ModuleWhat it brings
Mégapack Litethe content compendiums (weapons, spells, qualities, vehicles, NPCs…), without the text of the books; the system reads it first, and it is enough on its own (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.LY0gP2n4uytah6mP.JournalEntryPage.Qp5FrYdO1ggybgHp]{Mégapack entry})
Bibliothèque SR5the books as journals, to read a rule without leaving Foundry (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.LY0gP2n4uytah6mP.JournalEntryPage.foo9qJetkajRaK5n]{Bibliothèque entry})
Matrice v1Matrix House Rules, with the inside of hosts as a map (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.LY0gP2n4uytah6mP.JournalEntryPage.4V7hFPTyp4NVXfhI]{Matrice v1 entry})
Vertigea supplement of rules and content (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.LY0gP2n4uytah6mP.JournalEntryPage.g0O9ecLvjhjaIxvY]{Vertige entry})
Character Designer (Concepteur de personnage)guided character creation, step by step (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.LY0gP2n4uytah6mP.JournalEntryPage.FY83GXbOqmVz6WN9]{Character Designer entry})
Visual effects (SFX)the animations of shots, spells and explosions (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.LY0gP2n4uytah6mP.JournalEntryPage.T5p4QWSziZNI4xOL]{SFX entry})
Corporate topology (Topologie corporatiste)the map of the megacorporations, from one era to the next (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.LY0gP2n4uytah6mP.JournalEntryPage.hu1TCY7d5cZXfs3p]{Topology entry})
Revised martial arts (Arts martiaux révisés)a revision of martial arts, as House Rules (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.LY0gP2n4uytah6mP.JournalEntryPage.G5lt3ucuBihlzQCc]{revised martial arts entry})

References

pages.name: 0.3 The first launch of a world

text.content:
GM

What it is for

The first time a new world opens, the system asks you a single question: how far should it enforce the rules of the book? After that, all its settings are in a single window, Shadowrun settings.

Backlinks: @UUID[.97e4IWOiXu7XAeW3]{MENU}

← @UUID[.K6CX2EasFO6vz6Be]{0.2 Installing and updating} · @UUID[.aOF67Nbl48znk5T7]{The new world question} →

In a world that has never been opened with the system, the GM sees the new world window once. An existing world never sees it.

Step by step: choosing

  1. Read the three choices:

    • Automation: Advanced: where a rule of the book forbids an action, the system refuses it; it sets the "Running" state from the distance, moves the clock forward in combat and delivers purchases after their delay. This is the book, and the default choice.

    • Automation: Light: no refusal; the system lets things through, and the GM gets a discreet message at each deviation. Purchases arrive at once.

    • Automation: Custom: nothing is changed, and the Shadowrun settings window opens on the Presets tab.

  2. Tick your choice, then confirm. Closing the window without choosing applies Advanced.

This choice can be changed at any time, in the Presets menu (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.arMGpK6RvbR3sLNQ.JournalEntryPage.MxHL8At1JidYvFM3]{see 8.1}) or family by family in @UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.arMGpK6RvbR3sLNQ.JournalEntryPage.yj32FTBiKvVIyGIf]{the rule locks}.

Backlinks: @UUID[.97e4IWOiXu7XAeW3]{MENU} > @UUID[.Gfk5zUuTaOqS9vUv]{0.3 The first launch of a world}

← @UUID[.Gfk5zUuTaOqS9vUv]{0.3 The first launch of a world} · @UUID[.q5GXYM16NSmsFUJp]{The Shadowrun settings window} →

All the system's settings are sorted by tabs in a single window.

Step by step: opening it

  1. Open the Settings tab of the sidebar, then Configure Settings.

  2. In the system's section, click Open the settings.

  3. Pick a tab on the left, or type a word in the search field at the top: it finds a setting by its name or its description.

  4. Make your changes, then click Save Changes. If a setting requires a reload, a single question offers it; for a world setting, the players' pages reload too.

  • Each setting recalls its default value at the end of its description ("Default: unticked.").

  • A tag flags what departs from the core rulebook: book option (a printed optional rule) or house rule (a rule no book gives). Type "house" in the search to see them all.

  • Reset Defaults puts the values of a new world back into the window; nothing is saved before Save Changes (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.arMGpK6RvbR3sLNQ.JournalEntryPage.EVmnGJKbAtj857w9]{8.1}).

  • A player who opens the window only sees their own settings (PAN crown, interface).

The tabs

TabWhat you set there
Presetsan automation level and rules set in one go, your saved settings, and the rule locks: what the system refuses in the name of the book (GM only)
Interfacethe appearance, the hover help, the reminder of book pages (each for themselves, except the rule reminders)
Combat, Magic, Matrix, Riggingthe rule options of each domain
PAN crownthe crown of devices around tokens
Perception and visioncybereyes, vision ranges
Body, health and augmentationshealing, diseases, Essence, augmentations
Looting and spoils, Shoppickpocketing, looting bodies, buying, selling, delivery
Calendarthe world's clock
Gamemaster's toolsreference compendiums, factions, cons, tokens created during play, item effects
Otherthe encryption of commcode messages, a house rule (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.CKM0UvZC23LLnCgv.JournalEntryPage.6tBbo4KfG1RXgBmJ]{see 5.3})

The detail of each box: @UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.arMGpK6RvbR3sLNQ.JournalEntryPage.EVmnGJKbAtj857w9]{the Shadowrun settings window, tab by tab}.

References

  • wiki: System settings, wiki: GM's first steps.

Backlinks: @UUID[.97e4IWOiXu7XAeW3]{MENU} > @UUID[.Gfk5zUuTaOqS9vUv]{0.3 The first launch of a world}

← @UUID[.aOF67Nbl48znk5T7]{The new world question} · @UUID[.o25ieQmnMSZt0yYC]{0.4 The screen at a glance} →

All

What it is for

Before your first game, take five minutes to find your way around the screen. The Shadowrun 5 system adds a few buttons to Foundry's: a Sixth World clock at the top, the shop and the dealership in the right-hand bar, a crown of icons around each token and a help window that explains what you hover over. This chapter shows them to you, then points you to the chapter that details them.

  • ① The scene controls (left column): Foundry's tools for tokens, measuring, walls, lighting… The system adds the Chase tool to the token tools (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.5afKb26kGAzDG0I9.JournalEntryPage.Kyp3B3PN2QJ1zfc3]{chases}).

  • ② Scene navigation: the scene on display and, for the GM, the other prepared scenes.

  • ③ The Sixth World clock: the world's date and time, which the GM moves forward with a click (@UUID[.YRfJG9p6WnN6cUDi]{see below}).

  • ④ The sidebar: chat, combat, actors, items, journals, compendiums… and two buttons of the system, the Shop and the Dealership (@UUID[.mKZ6bak91UOPwDlM]{see below}).

  • ⑤ A token: click it to select it, right-click to open its HUD (@UUID[.9jXWevgNpySvo7Wz]{see below}).

  • ⑥ Connected players and the scene's environment: the list of connected people, and below it the Matrix Noise and the background count of the displayed scene, which are added automatically to rolls made on that scene.

  • ⑦ The macro bar: drag a weapon, a spell or a skill onto it from the sheet, and the system makes the button that rolls the test.

  • ⑧ Chat input: roll cards arrive in the chat tab, above it.

The GM and the player do not see the same screen

The player has neither the wall and lighting tools, nor the buttons that move the clock forward, nor the scenes the GM has not shown. Everything described here as "GM only" is simply absent from their screen.

Backlinks: @UUID[.97e4IWOiXu7XAeW3]{MENU}

← @UUID[.q5GXYM16NSmsFUJp]{The Shadowrun settings window} · @UUID[.mKZ6bak91UOPwDlM]{The sidebar} →

The column of icons on the right of the screen opens Foundry's tabs. The system slips two buttons into it, just above the Settings cog.

Step by step: opening the shop

  1. Hover over the cart icon: the tooltip shows Shop.

  2. Click it. The shop window opens; choose the buyer at the top of the window.

  3. To open it with your character already chosen as the buyer, go through their sheet instead: Gear tab, Shop button in the finances block.

The car-shaped button, just below, opens the Dealership: there you build a drone or a vehicle with its modifications and see its price before buying it. Both buttons are there for everyone, GM and player alike; what each can buy there depends on the GM's settings.

The detail: @UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.bqnSE0NCUfCmiCd8.JournalEntryPage.zKky8MvmSeq77inw]{the shop} and @UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.5afKb26kGAzDG0I9.JournalEntryPage.I5GXBTreZxunHsIW]{the dealership}.

A module adds a tab?

The tabs other modules add are placed before the Settings cog: the system always keeps it at the bottom of the column, just above the arrow that folds the bar.

Backlinks: @UUID[.97e4IWOiXu7XAeW3]{MENU} > @UUID[.o25ieQmnMSZt0yYC]{0.4 The screen at a glance}

← @UUID[.o25ieQmnMSZt0yYC]{0.4 The screen at a glance} · @UUID[.YRfJG9p6WnN6cUDi]{The clock and the calendar} →

At the top centre of the screen, the clock shows the world's date and time, for example Wednesday 1 January 2070 00:00:00. Everyone sees it; only the GM has the buttons that move it forward.

Step by step: moving the clock forward (GM)

  1. Click +1 min, +10 min, +1 h, +1 d or +1 wk. Several quick clicks add up: three clicks on +1 min make three minutes.

  2. To jump to a precise date, click the calendar icon at the end of the line (Go to a date), enter the date and time, then confirm.

Step by step: choosing your display (everyone)

  1. Click the crossed-out eye (Hide the calendar): only a small icon remains at the top of the screen; click it to reopen the clock.

  2. Click the calendar icon at the top right of the clock (Month view): the month grid opens under the clock, with the current day framed and the list of the month's events. The same button (Compact view) closes it.

This display choice belongs to each person and is kept from one session to the next. In combat, each new turn moves the clock forward by three seconds (Core Rulebook p. 49); the Calendar: combat advances the clock setting turns that off. The events, deadlines and deliveries that follow the clock are described in the chapter @UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.bqnSE0NCUfCmiCd8.JournalEntryPage.aK1sRuW82YTF1xdL]{on the calendar}.

Already using a calendar module?

If a calendar module is active (Simple Calendar Reborn, Seasons & Stars…), the system steps aside: it does not display its clock and lets that module handle the date. Durations, deadlines and deliveries keep following the world's time.

Backlinks: @UUID[.97e4IWOiXu7XAeW3]{MENU} > @UUID[.o25ieQmnMSZt0yYC]{0.4 The screen at a glance}

← @UUID[.mKZ6bak91UOPwDlM]{The sidebar} · @UUID[.9jXWevgNpySvo7Wz]{The token HUD} →

The HUD is the crown of buttons that surrounds a token when you right-click it. The system redraws it in its colours and adds the PAN button.

Step by step: targeting before attacking

  1. Right-click the opponent's token: the HUD opens.

  2. Click the target (Toggle Target State). The token now carries your target marker.

  3. Launch the attack from your sheet. The chat card then offers the defense to the targeted character.

Why target?

Almost every chain of the system starts from the target: it is the one that receives the defense button, then the resistance button. Without a target, the attack card has nobody to offer the response to, and the GM has to do the rest by hand.

The other buttons

  • Toggle Visibility State (GM): hides the token from the players, or shows it to them.

  • Assign Status Effects: opens the palette of states. They really act on the character's rolls; Dead marks them defeated in the combat, and their turn is skipped.

  • Toggle Combat State: adds the token to the current combat, or removes it.

  • Show or hide the PAN: opens the crown of the character's connected devices (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.CKM0UvZC23LLnCgv.JournalEntryPage.4tswtGQqbgDVe9IS]{the PAN crown}).

  • A Foundry shortcut: a double right-click on someone else's token targets it directly; the HUD opened by the first click closes again.

  • On a vendor's token, the GM has a Shop button that opens their stall; the player opens it with a double click or a right-click on the token, when the vendor is open (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.bqnSE0NCUfCmiCd8.JournalEntryPage.VJKiwMTDWIl9kXMx]{see 7.2}).

  • On a bag lying on the ground, one more button opens its contents without changing the selection: whoever searches stays whoever takes (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.hqT1pRAqlBA4yN9s.JournalEntryPage.FI0Yyn9xEWcJLmHX]{items}).

Backlinks: @UUID[.97e4IWOiXu7XAeW3]{MENU} > @UUID[.o25ieQmnMSZt0yYC]{0.4 The screen at a glance}

← @UUID[.YRfJG9p6WnN6cUDi]{The clock and the calendar} · @UUID[.onM6wQeM2Rn5e8sp]{Hover help} →

When help is on, a small window opens at the bottom left of the screen and explains the element of the sheet you hover over: what it is for, what a click on it does, and for a computed value, the detail of the computation (the base, then each bonus with its source). It is the quickest way to discover a sheet: move the mouse around, the help follows.

Step by step: turning help on or off

  1. Open the Settings tab (the cog at the bottom of the sidebar), then Configure Settings.

  2. In the system's section, click Open the settings: the Shadowrun settings window opens.

  3. Go to the Interface tab, tick or untick Show Help Window, then save. The page reloads.

This setting is personal: each person decides for themselves, and turning it off deprives nobody else. At a table discovering the system, leave it on; at a seasoned table, turn it off, and the sheet breathes better.

When help is on, the sheets' tooltips are shown there too, instead of floating near the mouse; where the sheet already has its own help text, that is what is shown. The window sits just above the list of connected people and rises with it when the list grows.

The reminder of book pages

Chat cards, roll windows, notifications and help cite the page of the book their computation rests on, for example "(SR5 p. 170, 182)" (French page numbers, see 0.1). A table that prefers lighter screens unticks Rule reminders, in the same Interface tab: this setting belongs to the world, set by the GM for everyone, and requires a reload. The rules apply the same way; only the page mentions disappear, including on cards already posted. Item descriptions do not change.

Backlinks: @UUID[.97e4IWOiXu7XAeW3]{MENU} > @UUID[.o25ieQmnMSZt0yYC]{0.4 The screen at a glance}

← @UUID[.9jXWevgNpySvo7Wz]{The token HUD} · @UUID[.Pr4eleOT7yPQN1jR]{Appearance: Shadowrun 5 and 6 themes} →

The look of the system's sheets and windows is chosen in a personal setting, Appearance: it only changes your screen, never anyone else's, and touches no rule.

Step by step: changing the appearance

  1. Open Shadowrun settings, Interface tab (see hover help, above).

  2. In Appearance, choose Shadowrun 5 Theme (the default) or Shadowrun 6 Theme, closer to the look of the sixth edition.

  3. Click Save Changes. The page reloads with the new look.

And Foundry's light or dark mode?

Foundry also offers a light or dark mode (Settings → Configure Settings → Configure Interface). The sheets keep their look in both modes: it is the Appearance above that decides how they look. The system's other windows (shop, dealership, chase, factions, presets, broker, messaging…) have the look of the Character Designer — night header, cyan capital titles, square-cornered buttons — and follow Foundry's mode: "daylight" in light mode, neon in dark mode. The system's dialogs (confirmations, choices, installing a part) wear the same outfit.

Each sheet can also be enlarged from its bottom right corner, and remembers its size from one opening to the next, per type of sheet and on your computer only (wiki: bars, monitors and windows).

Backlinks: @UUID[.97e4IWOiXu7XAeW3]{MENU} > @UUID[.o25ieQmnMSZt0yYC]{0.4 The screen at a glance}

← @UUID[.onM6wQeM2Rn5e8sp]{Hover help} · @UUID[.tf3RaZcBiA1euScW]{Related settings and references} →

What the system does on its own

  • It adds the Matrix Noise and background count of the token's scene to the roll.

  • It moves the clock forward by three seconds at each new combat turn (Core Rulebook p. 49).

  • It keeps the Settings cog at the bottom of the sidebar, whatever modules are active.

What the GM does by hand

  • Moves the clock forward outside combat, with a click, when time passes in the story.

  • Shows or hides tokens and scenes.

Related settings
